ipis:Zindi:5.2337716667,14.988365.name: Zindi
ipis:Zindi:5.2337716667,14.988365.type: Artisanal mining site — child labour observed
ipis:Zindi:5.2337716667,14.988365.desc: Field-visited by IPIS. Reported workers: 100. Children under 15 observed working at this site. IPIS has mapped these sites through repeat field visits, recording child labour, armed-group interference, worker numbers and minerals per site.

kilns:Brick kilns — 8 here:22.8173,89.59.name: Brick kilns — 8 here
kilns:Brick kilns — 8 here:22.8173,89.59.desc: 8 brick kilns annotated in this satellite tile. The position is the tile’s own reference point — the dataset records kilns as annotated boxes inside a satellite tile rather than as individual coordinates, so this locates them to within about a kilometre, not to a chimney. Detected from Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and hand-validated, from SentinelKilnDB — 62,671 kilns across the Indo-Gangetic Plain covering India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. Brick kilns are the most consistently documented bonded-labour sector in South Asia: the mechanism is the peshgi advance, worked off across a whole family at a rate that never clears. This is a site in a sector where forced or child labour is documented to concentrate. It is not evidence that this particular site uses it.
